article.title: Audacity 4.0 Ships With a Qt Rewrite, New Clip-Editing Model, and .aup4 Project Format
article.summary: Audacity 4.0 replaces the open-source audio editor's wxWidgets interface with Qt, adds a new clip-editing model, Workspaces, and a .aup4 project format, while dropping several Audacity 3 features.
article.body_markdown:
## Overview

Audacity, the open-source multi-track audio editor that the project's [official site](https://www.audacityteam.org/) credits with "100M+ downloads since 2000," released version 4.0.0 on September 3, 2026. The [GitHub release notes](https://github.com/audacity/audacity/releases/tag/Audacity-4.0.0) describe the update as one that "rebuilds the application interface on Qt and introduces many new quality-of-life improvements, including a new clip-editing model." The release is listed as the current "Latest" version on GitHub, following the Audacity 3.7.9 patch released September 1 and a beta cycle that included a 4.0.0 Beta 4 pre-release on August 28.

## What We Know

**A ground-up interface rewrite.** Audacity 4.0 replaces the toolkit behind its user interface. The [GitHub release notes](https://github.com/audacity/audacity/releases/tag/Audacity-4.0.0) state "the interface has been rebuilt on Qt, with native high-DPI rendering," and the [official Audacity 4 features page](https://www.audacityteam.org/audacity-4) says the application is "Built on Qt" and "runs natively on macOS, Windows and Linux." Before this release, according to [OMG! Ubuntu's](https://www.omgubuntu.co.uk/2026/06/audacity-4-0-beta) coverage of the 4.0 beta in June, "The audio editor's interface, built on wxWidgets since the project began, now runs in Qt." [OMG! Ubuntu's](https://www.omgubuntu.co.uk/2026/09/audacity-4-released) report on the stable release calls the change "more than a superficial – some would say much-needed – facelift, as the toolkit switch brings native HDPI scaling." [LWN.net](https://lwn.net/Articles/1092439/) similarly describes the update as a "rewritten interface using Qt."

**New ways to edit clips.** The GitHub release notes describe a "new clip-editing model." Clips can be selected by clicking a clip header, or by Shift-clicking to select several at once, and moving, trimming, and time-stretching now apply to all selected clips together. Clips can also be grouped — "Groups remain together when moved, copied, pasted or duplicated" — moved between mono and stereo tracks, and split with a dedicated tool bound to the S key. [OMG! Ubuntu's](https://www.omgubuntu.co.uk/2026/09/audacity-4-released) release-day report independently confirms "Easier clip selection" and "Clips grouping" functionality, along with the ability to move and trim multiple clips simultaneously.

**Workspaces and interface customization.** UI layouts can now be saved as Workspaces. According to the [Audacity 4 features page](https://www.audacityteam.org/audacity-4), "Each workspace changes the tools in your toolbar," and "It also swaps the ruler between seconds and bars and beats." The release also adds accent-color theming — "Choose an accent color and apply it throughout your app" — plus the ability to "Switch between light and dark themes, each with a high-contrast variant." [OMG! Ubuntu](https://www.omgubuntu.co.uk/2026/09/audacity-4-released) reports that toolbars and panels "can be moved, popped-out or closed."

**A new project file format.** Audacity 4.0 introduces the .aup4 project format. The GitHub release notes state simply that "Audacity 4 uses the new .aup4 project format," while [OMG! Ubuntu's](https://www.omgubuntu.co.uk/2026/09/audacity-4-released) release-day report adds that the format "stores preview thumbnails and new clip and appearance data." Older projects convert automatically: the update "converts Audacity 3.x .aup3 and older .aup files to the new format – a one way process as converted projects can't be saved to older formats," per OMG! Ubuntu.

**Features left behind, for now.** Both the [GitHub release notes](https://github.com/audacity/audacity/releases/tag/Audacity-4.0.0) and [OMG! Ubuntu](https://www.omgubuntu.co.uk/2026/09/audacity-4-released) list the same set of Audacity 3 features that did not carry over to 4.0: Time Tracks, Note/MIDI tracks, the Mixer, the Macro Manager and its scripting pipe, VAMP and LADSPA plugin hosting, and Play-at-speed. The release notes frame the omissions as temporary, saying the project is "working on adding them in future releases," and [LWN.net](https://lwn.net/Articles/1092439/) notes that "the release is not fully feature-compatible with the Audacity 3.x series." Plugin support in 4.0 covers "VST3, Nyquist, LV2 on Linux and Audio Units on macOS," according to the GitHub release notes; the Audacity 4 features page adds that "open-standard LV2 plugins load right alongside VST3 and Audio Units, with no wrappers required."

## What We Don't Know

The release notes give no timeline for when the removed features, such as Macro Manager scripting or VAMP/LADSPA plugin hosting, might return. Neither the GitHub release notes nor the official Audacity site publish a minimum system-requirements list alongside the 4.0.0 release.
